title: fix: stop unavailable chat widgets from flooding history reads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening an old chat with an unavailable Canvas widget can repeatedly request the same failed view whenever later chat events arrive or rows remount. Those requests also search the transcript before discovering that the widget file is gone, competing with other users' history and artifact reads.

## User Impact

Missing saved widgets keep their error visible until the page reloads or the agent creates a replacement. Temporary loading failures, including sandbox startup failures, retry at most five times with exponential backoff, then offer manual Retry. Successful widget responses are unchanged. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing request owner now retains terminal failures across row remounts, retires their event subscriptions, and preserves retry backoff. Its request bookkeeping moves into a focused sibling module to stay within the view owner's line limit. Successful HTML remains owned only by mounted views.

The server opens a document immediately after session admission, before searching for its transcript receipt. Missing files release the retained read without entering the shared history-worker pool. Existing files still require the same receipt authorization before any content is returned. Both view responses and dashboard imports consume the document already read by that owner, so successful imports perform one source read. Sandbox startup failures are marked retryable after a valid source read; missing sources retain their terminal classification. Source loading and host startup remain parallel. An admitted session reader now receives generic UNAVAILABLE for a nonexistent arbitrary ID before receipt lookup, while present unreferenced IDs remain FORBIDDEN; document IDs are random UUIDs, and this reveals no bytes or paths.

## Evidence

The synthetic production-bundle Control UI reproduction falls from 13 view requests after 12 later chat-final events to 1. The event/remount unit regression falls from 25 requests to 1. The transient-error regression falls from 45 requests to 6 total attempts. All three fail on the original behavior.

48 focused UI unit tests, 2 Chromium parking/lifecycle tests, 1 mock-Gateway browser E2E, and 48 Canvas server tests pass. Another 31 board tests pass; the dashboard-import work-count regression fails before the follow-up with two source reads and passes with one. The server regression creates a real saved receipt, removes its synthetic document, invokes the actual request route, and verifies UNAVAILABLE without transcript matching; it fails on base. Existing success, guest/branch/archive/revocation and sandbox behavior remain green.

Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against 66fc4d8848c5ab6ff3d29c8c5d093cfc5a95de7d: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Production and full-tree unused-file scans pass. All changed-file gates pass after targeted correction: the first full `pnpm check:changed` caught line-cap/format issues, fixed before the second run; the second full run passed every gate except an unknown event payload in the benchmark assertion. The corrected scripts typecheck and lint rerun passed. Core, all core test graphs, UI, scripts, SQLite guards, controller/i18n guards and dependency/import checks are covered. The final-head hosted Codex review was clean on the initial head. Hosted reviews found a sibling dashboard duplicate read and temporary host failures being classified as terminal. Both are fixed with base-red regressions, including actual WebSocket port-conflict recovery. Independent follow-up Codex autoreviews are clean through P3; ClawSweeper reviewed final head `95fb4283e352f972734d9a62c91b7e2378685407` with zero actionable findings and zero open items.

Runtime production LOC: +50. This implements terminal request state and finite retries in the existing owner and carries the already-read document through server authorization. Tests: +313. The rerunnable synthetic performance driver is separate from runtime production.

An additional real-Gateway WebSocket regression occupies the sandbox port, observes retryable UNAVAILABLE for an existing document and nonretryable UNAVAILABLE for a missing document, releases the port, and receives identical HTML. The identical test is red on c3d2601 and green with the classification fix. The UI recovery table proves no retry before 1,000 ms, then successful mounting.

The first CI run also exposed an inherited startup-test timing failure from #196482: cold chat preparation may yield before its row mounts. Controlled slow preparation reproduces the same missing-row assertion on the exact PR parent and CI main parent. The test now awaits the existing row with `waitForSolid`; all Retry/Discard assertions remain intact and the five-test file passes. No production startup behavior changed. The separate 18-error release-page markdownlint regression from #201913 is unchanged and documented in the CI attribution comment.

Related open work: #198629 changes widget loading presentation; #201028 adds widget-header inspection and extracts loading. This repair is limited to failed-read ownership and missing-source work.

### Performance

Acceptance recorded before measurement: remove all history-worker dispatches for missing documents; lower owner latency, CPU and allocation; retain successful behavior. The committed driver is `scripts/perf/canvas-missing-document-measure.ts`. Five interleaved before/after blocks, 20 warm reads per serial block; setup excluded. CPU includes worker threads; native allocation samples the actual synchronous scan in the measuring isolate in a separate run.

| Metric (median of five blocks) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Missing document owner p50 / p95 | 27.668 / 28.870 ms | 0.140 / 0.235 ms |
| Process CPU per read | 31,214 µs | 369 µs |
| Native scan-owner allocation per read | 6,555,076 B | 52,306 B |
| History-worker requests per 20 missing reads | 20 | 0 |
| Other session history p50 behind 32 missing views | 523.824 ms | 1.867 ms |
| History-worker requests per mixed burst | 33 | 1 |

Serial A/A p50: 27.640 / 27.881 ms (+0.87%); allocation A/A: 6,540,568 / 6,559,968 B (+0.30%); mixed A/A: 559.975 / 548.683 ms (−2.02%). Mixed block medians range 517.209–542.336 ms before and 1.728–2.036 ms after (two bursts/block; not a fleet-tail estimate). A separate CPU profile attributes 4,046 ms to the transcript scan subtree, primarily SQLite row iteration and row matching. Initial mixed measurements were excluded because only one worker was warm; the committed workload warms both before its A/A controls.

The synthetic fixture has 10,000 SQLite sessions and a 10,001-message selected transcript (118 MB database), running on macOS/APFS. This measures real history/file owners after session admission, not transport, a production Linux deployment or complete Gateway latency. The relevant scan is bounded by the selected transcript rather than total workspace size. The shared queue explains history/artifact contention; separate session-describe/send delays are not conclusively attributed by this proof.

Rerun with an absolute new fixture path: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/canvas-missing-document-measure.ts --fixture <path> --prepare`, then omit `--prepare` for timing; use `--mode allocation --native` for scan allocation or `--workload mixed --iterations 2` for queueing.

### Visual proof

Synthetic mock-Gateway content only; 1280 × 900, light theme. Before is 66fc4d8848c5a; after is 154f1c1cea68d991d6f488fe6ceb364331839f08. The runtime UI source is unchanged in subsequent server and test follow-ups. Clean before/after and annotated before/after follow.

![Before: unavailable widget offers Retry and later chat events repeat its read](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6b7eafe-7641-4eef-becb-1981fc16733b)

![After: terminal unavailable state remains visible without repeated reads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d75f8bc-5a2a-4027-aae4-00cbd28355ec)

![Before annotated: Retry is offered for a missing widget](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcf2610e-3414-456a-b0a0-28b5abeb3b46)

![After annotated: unavailable state stays visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be642288-8ed6-463d-8ade-29106636a33a)
## Final CI attribution

[CI run 44675298258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44675298258), attempt 1, completed at final head `95fb4283e352f972734d9a62c91b7e2378685407`. All selected checks except the two independently attributed main regressions and their aggregate passed, including both real-Gateway E2E shards and security-fast. CI remains failed; the maintainer explicitly authorizes pinned admin landing for proven inherited-only failures.

The 18 release-page MD001/MD024 errors reproduce identically on actual tested main parent `69eb76e6347b37573f91b01240e6b1d6c12871d2`. Restoration `72702a3600f77` / #201913 introduced them versus a clean predecessor. Release page and lint inputs are unchanged by this PR.

Browser shard 3 failed `community-invite-showing.e2e.test.ts:141`: after dismissal it expected Sessions focus, but CI's retained route was `/activity`. Exact-parent reproduction preserves runtime source and the original assertion: delaying the Activity module 300 ms and allowing its pending navigation to settle reproduces the same result. The test clicks Sessions while it remains selected, so the existing handler returns and Activity later commits; dismissal correctly focuses People. #199825 (`7701d7e404c61`) changed the test from a menu click to asynchronous People/Activity navigation without awaiting the route. #201038 (`a6983ed7eeb7`) introduced the current presented-page synchronization; #201208 (`62f44bc09d97`) retained the Sessions no-op in its new location. All five involved owner/test files are identical between main parent and tested merge. Normal passing replays are not offered as a fix. Waiting for Activity and then Chat via the existing route helper makes the same controlled reproduction green; that separate repair is recommended to the lead, not silently folded into this Canvas patch. Both failures are actionable main regressions, not noise.
